judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will terminate at the Manager's election upon the first to occur of' is internally contradictory — an automatic 'first to occur' trigger coupled with a discretionary election — and 'initial term' implies a further term that is never described.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c096 makes everything due on dissolution, and c077 measures a covenant from 'the second year of the Company's term' although this provision never fixes when the term begins.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'except for certain transfers to family trusts, to wholly-owned affiliates or by operation of law' uses 'certain' without saying which, leaving the carve-out's scope undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c004 states the transfer bar in absolute terms subject only to the Note Purchase Agreement, and c165 says transferability is 'severely restricted'; this partial carve-out is not reflected in either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'senior in priority as to either or both its payment or exercise' is awkward, and the Noteholders pre-agree to subordination 'on terms as required by the Manager' without any stated limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That open-ended subordination is hard to reconcile with c109's prohibition on permitting any Lien on the Collateral without a Majority in Interest, and with c012/c018's promise that the Notes are secured by the Company's assets.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'may not do... any of the following, among other restrictions' is a list expressly declared non-exhaustive, which defeats the expressio unius reading and leaves the protected class of actions indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its Lien prohibition conflicts with c108's pre-authorised senior Company Borrowing liens, and its 'Majority in Interest' (principal only) differs from c095's principal-plus-interest majority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'may form one or more new funds... or similar enterprises to the Company at any time and for any purpose' appears to be missing a word (competitive/similar to), and 'such of its business time... as may be necessary' is vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits competing funds without limit, which sits against c055's promise to allocate loan opportunities 'after consideration of all relevant factors' and c056's staffing assurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'such other Company reports and financial statements as the Manager, in its discretion, may determine' makes the reporting obligation almost entirely discretionary beyond tax information.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c167 confirms Noteholders are passive with no access to Company information; the two are consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'they will receive IRS Form 1099's only on a timely basis' is garbled word order but the meaning is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c018 and c123 also say Noteholders receive 1099s as creditors; c126 contemplates recharacterisation as members, which would upset this allocation, but that is expressly flagged as a contingency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is broken: 'may not be amended without the approval of a Majority in Interest of Noteholders (i) violates the Company's obligations...' omits the conditional ('if such amendment'), so the provision as written does not say what it means.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also refers to 'the Investor Documents', a capitalised term used nowhere else — c009 defines 'Offering Documents' and c081 defines 'Noteholder Agreements' — leaving the trigger undefined.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The general rule (Majority in Interest approval) is immediately followed by a proviso letting any single Noteholder waive or modify provisions as to his own Note with the Manager's consent, which largely undoes collective protection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That individual-waiver power sits against c089's pro rata payment covenant and c095's collective Collateral Agent regime, since individually varied Notes could break pro rata treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully drafted indemnity with a stated carve-out and an advancement undertaking; long but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its standard ('willful misconduct or gross negligence') differs from the standard c048 attributes to the Operating Agreement ('fraud, bad faith or willful misconduct'), a direct inconsistency about when indemnity is lost.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'except to the extent of their commitment to purchase Notes' is clear, and the trailing clause about impairment is merely explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c018 and c164; nothing elsewhere imposes Noteholder liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The power of attorney is granted by the Note Purchase Agreement but is described as covering 'documents that the Members have expressly agreed to execute' — Members, not Noteholders, which is the wrong party for a Noteholder power of attorney.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c097 and c018 make clear Noteholders are not Members, so a Noteholder power of attorney keyed to Members' agreements has no operative field.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies counsel (misspelling the firm as 'Greenburg Traurig') and disclaims representation of investors; the misspelling does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c057's lack-of-independent-representation disclosure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scope-limiting tax summary; the exclusions are enumerated and the reliance disclaimer is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c122 and c169's advice-to-consult provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition tracking the Internal Revenue Code's U.S. person definition; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in c119 and the following tax discussion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statement of partnership look-through with a recommendation to consult advisors; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No contrary provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard Circular 230 legend; formulaic and determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c119 and c169.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States an intention to treat the Notes as debt while conceding the characterisation binds neither the IRS nor 'any court' — a self-undercutting position, though openly disclosed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c018 flatly states Noteholders are secured creditors and not equity holders, while this and c126/c134 contemplate equity recharacterisation; the debt/equity question runs through the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company has selected 8% as its Comparable Yield' is definite, and the closing sentence expressly says the figure is not a projection of amounts payable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same 8% appears in c012 as a return target and in c016/c089 as a rate floor or average; a reader could conflate the tax convention with the payment obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical basis-and-character rule stated in conventional terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c124's contingent-debt treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Internally contradictory: it says that if Noteholders were characterised as members 'amounts received with respect to the Notes would not be treated as UBTI', then immediately describes circumstances in which such income 'would constitute debt financed property and generate UBTI'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because c108 and c164 expressly contemplate Company Borrowings, the debt-financed-property scenario is not hypothetical, and the provision's own reassurance cannot stand with c123's acknowledgement that recharacterisation is possible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional backup-withholding paragraph with a stated 28% rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No contrary provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory ERISA warning describing itself as 'a summary only'; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c129 and c169.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Advisory in nature; 'Plan Investors must make an independent investment decision... and must not rely upon the Manager' is a firm instruction but plainly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c002, c006 and c048's no-fiduciary theme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'structured so as not to subject the Fund' uses 'the Fund' where the defined term is 'the Company', and 'In the alternative, the Company expects to rely' is an odd way to state a primary exemption.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c003 and c170 restate the Investment Company Act position, and c170 coins yet another label, 'the Company Act', for the same statute this provision calls the 'Investment Company Act'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive risk disclosure about lender-status laws; 'may be deemed' hedges throughout but nothing operative turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c132-c134 and c155.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Discloses that 'the rates of interest to be paid to the Noteholders by the Company... may exceed the applicable statutorily-defined usury rates' and defines 'Interested Party' clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c089's 8% floor sits just below the 10% California threshold stated here, but c016/c012 contemplate 8% or more; whether the promised rate is lawful is a question the instrument raises against itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'may permit a borrower... to avoid paying principal and interest' is descriptive of statute; 'The Manager anticipates that such efforts should be sufficient' is soft but plainly hedged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c132 and c154; no operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Risk disclosure only; 'lender liability' is described as 'a developing and uncertain area of the law', which is candid rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its equitable-subordination discussion cuts against c018's assurance of secured creditor status, but it is expressly framed as a risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory sentence conceding that 'a summary of all possible risks is incomplete'; no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c026 and c185's qualification language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines 'Project' and describes typical borrower structure; 'Typically' hedges but nothing needs construing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Project' is used consistently through c137-c153.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Risk narrative; the phrase 'the inability of the Portfolio Manager to repay such Loan' uses 'Portfolio Manager' where 'Portfolio Borrower' is meant — a plain slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Portfolio Manager' appears nowhere else as a defined term; the intended referent is the Portfolio Borrower defined in c086.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Risk narrative about project history; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c161's no-operating-history disclosure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory list-stem ('Such risks include, among others') that is expressly non-exhaustive; risk disclosure only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Introduces c140-c146 consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Risk narrative with an illustrative list; no operative obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No contrary provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two lines of cost-overrun risk; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No contrary provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Environmental liability description; accurate and non-operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c153 notes the Company could become an owner by foreclosing on equity, which links to this risk without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extended leverage-risk narrative; hedged throughout but nothing ambiguous in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to c080 and c164 on Company-level leverage; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Uses 'the Project Owner' where the defined party is the Portfolio Borrower, and refers to first and second mortgages generically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c062 caps junior-lien loans at 20% of the Loan Portfolio, which this narrative does not mention; the mismatch is between a risk disclosure and a policy limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanics-lien narrative; 'must be negotiated by the Portfolio Borrower' is loosely put but the passage is descriptive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No contrary provision; c068's title insurance covers priority only, which fits.
